overview: Incumbent Mayor Stephanie Muccini Burke and challenger David McKillop, Sr. participated in a mayoral debate hosted by the Medford Chamber of Commerce and Tufts University. The candidates discussed city infrastructure, downtown parking, charter review, commercial development, housing affordability, public safety funding, the opioid crisis, and Complete Streets projects ahead of the November 7 municipal election.

items.title: Opening Statements
items.summary: Mayor Stephanie Muccini Burke and challenger David McKillop, Sr. presented opening statements outlining their professional backgrounds and campaign visions for Medford.

items.title: Primary City Issue
items.summary: McKillop cited density concerns and outdated zoning as the city's most critical challenge, while Burke identified aging infrastructure and road conditions.

items.title: Charter Review
items.summary: Both candidates expressed support for charter review, with Burke advocating for ward representation and McKillop calling for municipal term limits.

items.title: Downtown Parking System
items.summary: McKillop criticized the kiosk parking program and called for renegotiating the vendor contract, while Burke detailed recent adjustments, app fee reductions, and contract buyout costs.

items.title: Commercial Tax Base and Downtown Revitalization
items.summary: Burke pointed to mixed-use zoning and the Medford Square Master Plan to broaden the commercial tax base, while McKillop proposed creating a design review board and prioritizing direct waterfront development.

items.title: Housing Affordability
items.summary: McKillop proposed senior tax relief and middle-income housing initiatives, while Burke highlighted inclusionary zoning proposals and transit-oriented development.

items.title: Public Library and Police Station Funding
items.summary: Burke defended securing state grant funding and foundation support for a new library alongside active police station planning, while McKillop argued public safety facilities should have been prioritized first.

items.title: Opioid Crisis Response
items.summary: McKillop called for more frequent community task force meetings and school involvement, while Burke highlighted grant-funded school education, union trades outreach, and the hiring of a municipal recovery coach.

items.title: Public Safety Staffing
items.summary: Burke explained that transitioning 911 dispatch to civilian personnel will return officers to street patrol, while McKillop advocated for proactive staffing formulas tied to population growth.

items.title: Arts and Cultural Strategy
items.summary: McKillop suggested establishing citywide art and music festivals, while Burke cited the management contract for the Chevalier Theater, local art displays at City Hall, and planned dedicated art space.

items.title: Sanctuary City Policy
items.summary: Burke highlighted Medford's welcoming city resolution and local police procedures regarding federal reporting, while McKillop voiced support for existing law enforcement practices.

items.title: Traffic Calming and Complete Streets
items.summary: McKillop raised safety concerns about narrow shared bicycle lanes, while Burke reviewed completed Complete Streets projects on Boston Avenue and upcoming improvements in Haines Square.

items.title: Community Inclusivity and Engagement
items.summary: Burke emphasized respectful public discourse and broad community participation, while McKillop advocated for wider public input on major decisions including Community Preservation Act funds.

items.title: Closing Statements
items.summary: McKillop and Burke delivered closing statements urging voters to support their respective approaches to city leadership in the upcoming election.
